If you’re looking specifically for a **blue Staffordshire Bull Terrier (“Staffy”) puppy near Glasgow**, I’d start with established breed-club/Kennel Club channels rather than generic puppy-sale ads.

### Where to look

- **The Royal Kennel Club – Find a Puppy:** their current Staffordshire Bull Terrier listings can be filtered by location and health testing. Blue is a recognised breed-standard colour. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 
 [royalkennelclub.com](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Champdogs:** currently lists Staffordshire Bull Terrier breeders in Scotland, including breeders around **Cumbernauld** and Edinburgh, with health-testing information. [Champdogs](https://www.champdogs.co.uk/breeds/staffordshire-bull-terrier/breeders?ct=Scotland&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 
 [champdogs.co.uk](https://www.champdogs.co.uk/breeds/staffordshire-bull-terrier/breeders?ct=Scotland&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- The **Scottish Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club** is another useful route to reputable breed contacts; the Southern Counties SBT Society's puppy-buying guidance lists it among the UK breed clubs. [SC Staffordshire Bull Terrier Society](https://www.scsbts.com/sbt-welfare-and-rescue/buying-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

I would **not choose a breeder simply because they advertise “blue”**. The Royal Kennel Club explicitly says colour should be secondary to health and temperament. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

### Questions I'd ask the breeder

Before paying a deposit, ask:

1. **“Can I see the puppy with its mother, at your home?”**
 You want to see where the litter is actually being raised and observe the dam's temperament.
2. **“Can I see the parents' original health-test results?”**
 For Staffies, ask specifically about:

 - **HC-HSF4 hereditary cataracts**
- **L-2-HGA**
- **BVA/KC elbow testing**
- **BVA/KC/ISDS eye testing**, including litter eye screening
 These are among the health tests recommended by the Royal Kennel Club for the breed. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
3. **“Have the puppies had their eyes clinically screened?”**
 The Staffordshire Bull Terrier breed-club guidance specifically recommends litter eye screening before puppies leave. [SC Staffordshire Bull Terrier Society](https://www.scsbts.com/sbt-welfare-and-rescue/buying-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
4. **“What are the parents' KC registration numbers and health results?”**
 You can independently check KC health information rather than relying on a breeder's screenshot or verbal assurance.
5. **“What is the puppy's inbreeding coefficient, and what is the breeding history of the parents?”**
6. **“What socialisation have the puppies had?”**
 Ask about children, household noises, handling, other dogs, car journeys, grooming, etc.
7. **“What vaccinations, microchipping and worming have been done, and what paperwork comes with the puppy?”**
8. **“Will you take the dog back or help rehome it if I can no longer keep it?”**
 A responsible breeder should remain interested in the dog's welfare after the sale.

### A couple of red flags

I'd be particularly cautious if the seller:

- wants a deposit before letting you see the puppy and its mother;
- won't provide **verifiable** health-test results;
- has several different breeds or many litters available simultaneously;
- insists on meeting in a car park or another location rather than their home;
- focuses heavily on “rare blue,” oversized, huge-headed, or unusual-looking Staffies;
- has puppies available constantly;
- is reluctant to let you ask questions.

And don't let the word **“KC registered”** substitute for health testing. Registration tells you about pedigree/registration; it isn't itself a guarantee that the puppy or parents are free of inherited disease.

If you tell me **how far from Glasgow you're willing to travel (e.g. 30, 60 or 100 miles)** and whether you want **male or female**, I can search the current Scottish listings and give you a shortlist of blue Staffy litters/breeders to investigate.
